result:
Rebase on a shared branch only when everyone agrees and nobody else has based work on the commits you'd rewrite. Rebase rewrites history, so it forces others to reconcile.

Use rebase when:
- Your own unpushed or private commits need to sit on top of the latest shared branch before you push. Run `git pull --rebase`.
- You want to tidy local commits (squash, reword) before sharing them.
- The team has agreed to a rebase workflow and force-pushes with `--force-with-lease`.

Use merge when:
- Others have already pulled the branch. Rewriting pushed commits breaks their clones.
- You want to preserve the true history and avoid force-pushing.

Rule: never rebase commits others already have.
